Definition: from G4862 and G2186; to stand up together, i.e. to resist (or assault) jointly:--rise up together.
BiblicalUsage: At Philippi the multitude rises up together against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates tear off their clothes and command them to be beaten. A crowd rising as one body against two men is the shape persecution often takes, and it falls on the servants of Christ first.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a multitude can rise together against the truth, and I believe standing in it, as Paul and Silas did, is worth more than the crowd's approval.
